author: Bianca Caputo
title: $20M in NYS budget agreement aimed at Albany budget deficit - NewsBreak
text:
By Bianca Caputo ,
1 hours ago
ALBANY, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) — $20 million dollars in the New York State budget agreement is geared specifically to filling Albany’s budget deficit.
Albany Mayor Dorcey Applyrs first spoke about the city of Albany’s budget crisis in March. She’s denied that she knew about the budget gap before taking office, after serving as city auditor during the previous administration.
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Since learning about the budget crisis, the Applyrs administration has saved $7.6 million, implemented a hiring pause, limited non-essential spending and asked city departments to create spending reduction plans.
Assemblymember Gabriella Romero (D) who represents Albany said when she heard about the city’s fiscal situation, she knew extra aid was needed for Albany to recover. Senator Patricia Fahy said she was surprised by the shortfall.
“It’s been shocking to me, as well as to many others,” said Fahy.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! Fahy said struggles with cuts in federal funding and expiring COVID-19 relief funds have created a unique situation for the Capital City and other municipalities.
“Many upstate cities have hit what they call a COVID cliff,” said Fahy.
The funding is part of more than $40 million in aid coming from New York State to Albany. Fahy said this support is needed to stabilize the city and voter confidence.
“Give us a chance here, give the new mayor a chance,” said Fahy. “If the heart, if the core of the Capital Region suffers, the whole region suffers.”
Menands firefighters, community groups push forward after fire In a statement, the Albany Common Council said the funding will give the city, “…time to address the existing deficit without resorting to drastic and immediate austerity measures that would harm the safety and quality of life of city residents.”
A statement from Applyr’s office said the mayor will continue to look at cost saving measures like cuts to departments and reductions in overtime to ensure the city isn’t in this fiscal position again.
Former College of Saint Rose library collection up for auction The state funding isn’t earmarked for specific use, but Representative John McDonald (D) said he and other legislators will keep in contact with the city administration to make sure money is properly used.
“It’s not an open checkbook by any stretch of the imagination, but it’s not restricted either,” said McDonald. “We want to help and work with them on that, not telling them what to do, but to work with them and see what other support they need from the state.”
Albany will be asked to give a report at the end of the year on where money was used.
